Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Oct 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a couple hundred miles southwest of Manzanillo,
Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Tue Oct 27 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 272050
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Tue Oct 27 2026
 
...VANCE HOLDING STEADY OFFSHORE OF SOUTHWESTERN MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.2N 108.3W
ABOUT 290 MI...465 KM WSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 280 MI...450 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 17.2 North, longitude 108.3 West. Vance is
moving toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A gradual turn
toward the north is expected through midweek.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next couple of
days, and Vance could become a post-tropical cyclone during this
time if it is unable to sustain organized convection.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 70 miles (110 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4 
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, western Durango, 
and northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches 
possible over central and southern Sinaloa. This rainfall may 
produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep 
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southern, southwestern, and west-central Mexico during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Tue Oct 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 272051
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 PM MST Tue Oct 27 2026
 
Significant westerly wind shear and a dry mid-level environment are 
substantially impacting Vance this afternoon. Deep convection 
remains disorganized and displaced from the fully exposed low-level 
center, with the deepest thunderstorms located 50-100 mi east of the 
center. Recent objective and subjective satellite intensity 
estimates range from 26-36 kt. However, a recent METOP-B 
scatterometer pass indicated tropical-storm-force winds northeast 
and southeast of the center, and this was instrumental in 
determining the wind radii for this advisory. Based on the data, 
the intensity is maintained at 35 kt for this advisory.
 
Vance is moving northwestward at 305/08 kt, guided by a low-level
ridge centered over the south-central United States. A gradual turn
toward the north is forecast over the next couple of days as a
strong mid-level trough moves down the U.S. West Coast. This
steering pattern would bring Vance toward the entrance of the Gulf
of California by Thursday. The latest NHC track forecast has been
shifted slightly to the left and lies near the latest HFIP corrected
consensus aid (HCCA).
 
Despite moving over warm sea surface temperatures of 29-30 C over
the next couple of days, an increase in already significant wind
shear may offset any potential strengthening. However, intensity
guidance remains mixed, so the NHC forecast follows a consensus
approach and calls for no net change through midweek, although some
fluctuations are possible during this period. Vance is already
struggling to maintain organized deep convection near its center,
and simulated satellite imagery from the GFS and ECMWF suggests that
organized convection could become difficult to sustain by early
Thursday. Therefore, the latest NHC forecast calls for Vance to
become post-tropical by 36 h and degenerate into a remnant low by 60
h, around the time of its closest approach to west-central Mexico.
If Vance is unable to sustain organized convection closer to its
center, the transition to a post-tropical cyclone could occur even
sooner than currently forecast. Given this forecast, the threat of
tropical storm conditions over land remains low at this time.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern
Sinaloa, western Durango, and northwestern Nayari, especially in
areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of
Mexico and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  27/2100Z 17.2N 108.3W   35 KT  40 MPH

 24H  28/1800Z 19.7N 108.9W   35 KT  40 MPH
